finding.text: The "Data: how it's written" page (`public/framework/ai/overview.js:75-85`) says the owner's ask named 9 routes, but the source brief it's built from says something different: `public/framework/ai/2026-10-02/jsonl-writers/requirements.md:5` reads "twelve `.jsonl` writers exist... Five gaps let an unchecked line into a live file," not 9 routes / 4 gaps. The page is honest that it isn't exhaustive (it names the 20-plus-call-site grep), but it never reconciles the 12-vs-9 and 5-vs-4 numbers sitting one task-folder apart — worth a line saying what the missing ones are, or dropping the "12" framing so two different totals aren't both on the record.

In `render_writers` (`public/framework/ai/overview.js:76-80`), the "checked?" cell is built as `w.ok ? span.c("pass","yes") : span.c("fail","no")` — a direct call, not wrapped in `() => ...`. `span.c()` appends itself to whatever View is capturing at the moment the array is built (View.js:22), before `table()` ever runs, and only lands in the right `<td>` because `appendChild` re-parents an existing node. It happens to work (the same pattern is already used in `render_models`'s `fmt_rung`, `overview.js:351`), but `allRows` right below it (`overview.js:386-389`) wraps the equivalent case in a lazy `() => small.c(...)` specifically to avoid this — the two nearby examples disagree on the safe way to do it, so a future edit could easily copy the fragile one.

All paths and links the new code points to checked out: `file_link()`'s 9 target files exist, `page-item-design.md` and `page-extends-item/requirements.md` exist, `Tail.js`, `ext/Saver`, `ext/filesystem`, `ext/JSONL` and `dev/Socket` all resolve, and `data`/`saving` are correctly added to `SYSTEM_PARTS` (overview.js:19) so their tabs route. Deliverables 1 (the map), 4 (skills/roles/readmes) and 5 (tasks/cards/asks) were already live on the System tab before this task from earlier same-day work (the GROUPS/CONCEPTS cards, "Who starts the agents," and the `claude-md` page's task/asks cards) — this diff only had to add 2 (data writers) and 3 (how a page saves), which it does, so the five-part ask is met as a whole without duplicating anything.
